name: Amandari
insider_take: Hidden among ancient rice terraces, this sacred sanctuary feels like discovering Bali's best-kept secret—where traditional village life unfolds just beyond your villa's stone walls.
whats_special: Amandari sits on the edge of the Ayung River gorge, offering unobstructed views of Ubud's UNESCO-protected rice paddies that have been cultivated for over 1,000 years. The resort's design mirrors a traditional Balinese village, with each suite built as a standalone pavilion using local alang-alang grass roofing and Palimanan stone—the same materials used in nearby Hindu temples.
pro_tip: Book the Valley Suite for sunrise yoga on your private terrace—the morning mist rising from the rice fields creates an otherworldly meditation experience that's pure Instagram gold.
dont_miss: The nearby Gunung Kawi temple complex, featuring 11th-century rock-cut shrines carved directly into cliffsides—it's a 10-minute walk through working rice fields. Also, time your visit during harvest season (March-April) when farmers still use traditional methods and water buffalo, creating scenes unchanged for centuries.
pros: Stunning rice terrace views and authentic Balinese village atmosphere
Exceptional spa treatments and wellness programs in serene setting
Private pool villas with traditional Balinese architecture and modern luxury
World-class dining featuring local ingredients and international cuisine
cons: Remote location requires transportation for exploring broader Ubud area
